subject: LaunchForge commit cadence and threshold guardrails — proposal and questions
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir@launchforge.com>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.ai
Cc: Priya Shenoy <priya.shenoy@launchforge.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Launch cadence + discounts question

Alex — thanks for the time earlier. Quick follow-up with more detail on our launch: we expect a hard launch week of Oct 12 with a pre-launch beta in September. Traffic profile: baseline 20M tokens/month, jump to ~150M tokens during a 6-week ramp (peak weeks 3–6 after launch), and recurring seasonality with a Q4 peak (roughly +2.5x baseline).

Our procurement asks: we want a monthly committed model (for predictable billing) but need a way to preserve flexibility for the early weeks (we anticipate overshoot). Two specific asks:
1) Can Redwood support a graduated monthly commit where the first two months are smaller and step up to the committed tier in month 3? We prefer per-token discounts that increase with committed bucket size rather than flat blended discounts.
2) Any guardrails for seasonality surges — e.g., temporary burst allowance or true-up windows — so we don't immediately breach commit and get charged at list price.

If you can send a sample cadence and what discounts look like by bucket (and any sample invoice), that would help our finance and procurement teams sign off.

Thanks,
Samir
Head of Platform
LaunchForge

Attachment: launch_traffic_summary.csv (csv, 28KB)

From: alex_martinez@redwood.ai
To: Samir Rao <samir@launchforge.com>
Cc: Priya Shenoy <priya.shenoy@launchforge.com>, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-30T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Launch cadence + discounts question

Samir — great detail, this is helpful. I took a pass with Monica and sketched a pragmatic cadence you could adopt. High-level:

- Month 0 (beta / pre-launch): commit 10M tokens, per-token rate = $0.0022 (no discount tier)
- Month 1 (initial launch): commit 50M tokens, per-token list $0.0020, tiered discount kicks in at 50M+
- Month 2: commit 100M tokens, per-token list $0.0018 with the following buckets:
   * 0–49M: $0.0020
   * 50–199M: $0.0016 (20% discount blended for this bucket)
   * 200M+: callout pricing / enterprise tier
- Seasonality: 2-week burst allowance equal to 30% of monthly commit (no penalty) and a 30-day true-up window at month-end to reconcile overage before applying list rates.

We attached a proposed calendar (LF-Proposed-commit-calendar-v2.pdf) and a sample invoice showing how a true-up would appear (sample-invoice-LaunchForge-1.pdf). Notes:
- We can structure the discounts as per-bucket stepped pricing (so each bucket has its own per-token rate) which looks better for forecasted sharp ramps.
- If you need a safety net for Q4 seasonality we can add a one-time seasonal buffer that auto-triggers for Nov–Dec with pre-agreed thresholds and a small uplift to the committed fee.

Can you confirm if your finance team needs an invoice with month-by-month breakdowns vs. a single blended invoice? Also, what's the internal approval deadline — that helps prioritize a contract draft.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0123

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: Samir Rao <samir@launchforge.com>, alex_martinez@redwood.ai
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-31T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Launch cadence + discounts question

Samir — adding a couple practical clarifications from ops/finance:

- Billing cadence: Redwood invoices monthly with line items for committed tokens, actual tokens consumed, and any true-up adjustments. We can produce a month-by-month invoice (detailed) or a consolidated invoice; both formats are supported.
- Credits vs. refunds: we prefer issuing credits that apply to the next invoice for overages resolved in the true-up window. If you require cash refunds, that needs legal approval and will lengthen negotiation.
- SLA / dedicated capacity: we can offer a launch-priority queue as an add-on for the launch window (guaranteed throughput and prioritized routing) — we'd need to size GPU reservations 3–4 weeks ahead.

Action items for LaunchForge: send your internal approval deadline and confirm whether credits vs. refund is a hard requirement. Also pinged Dev to confirm whether a pilot week with higher burst (no charge) is OK from a capacity standpoint.

-Monica
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Launch cadence + discounts question

Alex/Monica — this looks promising. A few quick answers:
- Finance would like a month-by-month detailed invoice for the first 6 months to reconcile budgets.
- Refunds are preferable but not a hard blocker; if credits are the default we can accept that for the pilot and then revisit for long-term commitments.
- Approval deadline: Sept 14 — we'd like a signed contract and invoice sample before then.
- SLA: yes, we want the launch-priority queue. Can you send estimated costs for the reservation and how it maps to committed tokens?

Priya from procurement will manage redlines; copied her here.

Thanks,
Samir

Samir — Dev here (in infra/sizing). Quick technical confirmation: we can reserve a launch-priority pool sized to handle your expected 150M tokens/week peak (we'd map that to GPU-hours and an explicit reservation cost). Rough estimate: $18k/week for a 3-week reservation to cover the critical ramp (includes priority routing + KV cache pre-warming).

Proposal:
- Pilot month: allow up to 40% burst above committed tokens for no extra charge during beta/launch week (we'll flag usage in real-time).
- Month 1–3: graduated committed buckets as Alex outlined; automatic 30-day true-up; 30% monthly burst allowance.
- SLA add-on: one-time reservation fee (as above) + a per-token reduced overage rate for the reservation period.

I'll add a short sizing note to the drive folder and tag the implementation team once you confirm dates.

-Dev
